predecessors.note: Suruga and Tōtōmi, the home provinces where the Imagawa were shugo (clan page; the dates are not given). Cliopatria's Warring States Japan row draws all Japan as one shape; the daimyo domains are internal units.

successors.note: Mikawa from 1561-1565 and Tōtōmi from 1568-1569 (Ieyasu page).

rulers.name: Imagawa Yoshimoto
rulers.title: head of the clan
rulers.note: Succeeded after Ujiteru died suddenly in 1536; killed at Okehazama on 12 June 1560 (infobox).

rulers.name: Imagawa Ujizane
rulers.title: head of the clan
rulers.note: 'Ujizane succeeded to family headship after Yoshimoto's death, but the Imagawa clan fell from power.' The pages date his loss of Suruga to Takeda 1568-1569 only through the Takeda dossier.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for a daimyo domain Cliopatria lacks (Warring States Japan draws all of Japan as one shape). Home provinces Suruga, Tōtōmi and Mikawa (infobox); the clan were shugo of Suruga and Tōtōmi (no date). The 45 km circle at Shizuoka (Suruga, about 5,300 km2) and the 40 km circle at Hamamatsu (Tōtōmi, about 5,100 km2) are the same stand-ins the Takeda and Tokugawa dossiers use. 1536: Yoshimoto succeeded after the Hanagura Disturbance; 1540 the Hōjō invaded Suruga and were beaten.

1542: Yoshimoto advanced into Mikawa and lost the first battle of Azukizaka; 1548: he won the second against Nobuhide; he 'wrested control over the Suruga, Totomi, and Mikawa provinces' and 'continued to expand his territory until 1560' (page; no separate year). Eastern Aichi (12 cells) stands for Mikawa; the Muraki Castle in southeast Owari of 1554 is not drawn.

minus.text: Kaminogō and the Okazaki area of Mikawa

correction.text: Suruga, Tōtōmi and Mikawa without Kaminogō

keyframe_review.note: 1561: Matsudaira Motoyasu 'openly ended his allegiance to the Imagawa clan and captured Kaminogō castle' (Ieyasu page). Okehazama (12 June 1560) had already killed Yoshimoto.
By 1565 Ieyasu was 'master of all of Mikawa Province' (citation needed on the page); the Imagawa keep Suruga and Tōtōmi.

1567: Shingen and Ieyasu 'occupied former Imagawa territory'; 1568: Shingen invaded Suruga; 1569: he 'secured Suruga' and Ieyasu captured Horikawa Castle in Tōtōmi (Ieyasu page). The Imagawa clan page: 'Within a decade the clan lost its land to the Tokugawa and Takeda'.

ledger.note: 1536: Ujiteru died suddenly, Yoshimoto succeeded after the Hanagura Disturbance ('the Genkō faction was eliminated'). The year is the page's; the extent is the researcher's reading of the home provinces (the clan page gives no dates for the shugo posts).

1548: the second battle of Azukizaka won against Nobuhide; 'wrested control over the Suruga, Totomi, and Mikawa provinces' in the following decades and 'continued to expand his territory until 1560'. The page gives no separate year for Mikawa; the date is bridged to 1548, confidence 1.

region.text: Kaminogō and the Okazaki area of Mikawa

ledger.note: 1561: Matsudaira Motoyasu 'openly ended his allegiance to the Imagawa clan and captured Kaminogō castle'. The Tokugawa clan page puts the break in 1566.

minus.text: Kaminogō and the Okazaki area of Mikawa

ledger.note: By 1565: 'Ieyasu had become the master of all of Mikawa Province' (citation needed on the page).
1568: Shingen invaded Suruga; in 1567 he and Ieyasu 'came to terms and occupied former Imagawa territory'.
1569: 'secured Suruga after defeating Hōjō Ujimasa's forces' (the page's wording).
1569: Suruga is Takeda land (Shingen page); the Takeda dossier carries the mirror gain.

1568-1569: Ieyasu 'besieged the Horikawa Castle in Tōtōmi' in 1568 and captured it in 1569; 1570 Hamamatsu. The Imagawa clan page: 'Within a decade the clan lost its land to the Tokugawa and Takeda'; the pages do not say how much of Tōtōmi went in 1569.

1569: the last Imagawa land goes. The clan survived as kōke (masters of ceremonies) to the Tokugawa in the Edo period (clan page); the infobox says the clan 'ruled until 1560', the date of Yoshimoto's death.

wars.name: Imagawa–Hōjō conflict over Suruga
wars.outcome: 'The Later Hōjō clan invaded into the Suruga province but Yoshimoto defeated the Hōjō's force'; peace with the Hōjō came in 1554 through the marriage of Yoshimoto's son Ujizane.

wars.name: Imagawa advance into Mikawa and Owari
wars.outcome: The first battle of Azukizaka (1542) was lost, the second (1548) won against Nobuhide; in 1554 the Imagawa built Muraki Castle in southeast Owari.

wars.name: Battle of Okehazama
wars.outcome: Yoshimoto was killed on 12 June 1560 by an Oda force of 2,000-3,000 against his 25,000 (page estimates); the Imagawa were greatly weakened.

wars.name: Takeda invasion of Suruga
wars.outcome: Takeda secured Suruga in 1569; the Hōjō intervened and won at Mimasetoge in 1569; Fukazawa fell in 1571.

wars.name: Tokugawa campaign in Tōtōmi
wars.outcome: Horikawa Castle besieged in 1568 and captured in 1569.

certainty.note: The pages name castles, provinces and battles, not borders; Suruga and Tōtōmi are circles and Mikawa is Aichi without Owari.

sources.title: Imagawa clan
sources.note: Home provinces Suruga, Totomi and Mikawa; shugo of Suruga and Totomi (undated); Yoshimoto in the 1540s and 1550s tried to make the clan strongest in eastern Japan, castles in Suruga, Totomi, Mikawa and Owari; Okehazama 1560; within a decade the clan lost its land to the Tokugawa and Takeda; ruled until 1560 (infobox); kōke in the Edo period.

sources.title: Imagawa Yoshimoto
sources.note: 1536 succession and the Hanagura Disturbance; 1540 helped Shingen imprison Nobutora, the Hojo invaded Suruga and were defeated; 1542 advance into Mikawa, Azukizaka lost; 1548 Second Azukizaka won against Nobuhide; wrested control of Suruga, Totomi and Mikawa, expanding to 1560; 1554 Muraki Castle in southeast Owari; 1554 peace with the Hojo; died 12 June 1560 at Okehazama; Ujizane succeeded and the clan fell from power.

sources.title: Battle of Okehazama
sources.note: 12 June 1560 in Owari; Oda defeated the Imagawa; Matsudaira Motoyasu, an Imagawa retainer, pledged fealty to Oda; the Imagawa greatly weakened and soon destroyed by neighbours.

sources.title: Takeda Shingen
sources.note: 1567 Shingen and Ieyasu occupied former Imagawa territory; 1568 Shingen invaded Suruga; 1569 secured Suruga.

sources.title: Tokugawa Ieyasu
sources.note: 1561 openly ended allegiance to the Imagawa and captured Kaminogo castle; by 1565 master of all Mikawa; 1568 Horikawa Castle in Totomi besieged, captured 1569.

notes: Written by jk-01-x on 2026-10-19 from five pages (Imagawa clan, Imagawa Yoshimoto, Battle of Okehazama, Takeda Shingen, Tokugawa Ieyasu). A Sengoku daimyo domain inside Cliopatria's single Warring States Japan row. The pages are thin on years: the clan page gives no date for the shugo posts of Suruga and Tōtōmi, the Yoshimoto page gives the 1536 succession, 1540, 1542, 1548 and 1554 events but no year for the acquisition of Mikawa, and the fall of the clan rests on the Takeda and Tokugawa pages (1561-1565 Mikawa, 1568-1569 Suruga and Tōtōmi). The dossier opens at 1536 and closes at 1569 (the clan page's infobox says the clan 'ruled until 1560'). Not on the pages: Ujizane's flight and the fall of Kakegawa, the Suruga capital, the 1554 Kai-Sagami-Suruga alliance (the Yoshimoto page has only the Hōjō peace of 1554; the three-way alliance appears in the 1560 campaign narrative), the Anjō event of 1549, Tōtōmi's boundaries. Counterpart strings 'takeda-clan', 'tokugawa-clan', 'later-hojo-clan' and 'oda-clan' exist; 'Oda Nobuhide' is a person (the Oda dossier opens at 1551). The Tokugawa dossier carries Mikawa from 1561. The Takeda dossier counts Suruga as gained from 'imagawa-clan' in 1569. Area comparison not applicable (no infobox area).
